Family: Ailiidae. Adult size: 13.0 cm. Temperature: 23-26°C. pH: 6.5-7.2. IUCN Red List: Not Evaluated.

Eutropiichthys cetosus is still listed in FishBase as belonging to the Schilbeidae family but is updated in The Catalog of Fishes as a member of the Ailiidae family.
Asia: Kaladan River drainage in southern Mizoram, India.
Found in a clear, slow and moderate flowing river with a depth of 1-4 m.

Dorsal spines (total): 2; dorsal soft rays (total): 7; anal soft rays: 48-54; vertebrae: 49-52. Eutropiichthys cetosus is distinguished from all congeners, except E. burmannicus, by having more gill rakers (25-35 vs. 15-20) on the first gill arch. It differs from E. burmannicus by a moderately rounded snout in lateral view (vs. distinctly pointed) and slightly trilobed in dorsal view (vs. acutely angular), a deeper head relative to its length (68.7-77.1% HL vs. 65.4-67.5% HL), fewer branched pectoral-fin rays (13-15 vs. 15-17), and a more slender body (depth at dorsal-fin origin 19.2-23.5% SL vs. 23.7-25.3% SL; depth at anal-fin origin 17.5-23.5% SL vs. 23.2-26.3% SL). (Ng et al 2014).

Etymology: the genus name Eutropiichthys comes from Greek eutropheia = well fed + Greek ichthys = fish. The specific name cetosus derives from the Latin adjective cetus, a large sea animal (commonly a whale), alluding to the numerous gill rakers of this species, reminiscent of baleen in baleen whales.
